issues.legal_issue: A compromise deed granting property to a widow in unqualified terms of absolute ownership confers an absolute estate when its language and context do not qualify the grant.
material_facts: The compromise deed stated that the properties allotted to the widow were to be enjoyed by her as “Malik Mustakil.”
The widow gave up claims to a substantial portion of the disputed property in return for an absolute interest in the portion allotted to her.
The deed’s language and the circumstances of the compromise did not qualify the estate granted.
issues.conclusion: The widow received an absolute estate in the properties allotted to her under the compromise.
issues.legal_principle: A document is ordinarily construed according to the normal and natural meaning of its words. Dhyan Singh v. Jugal Kishore and Bishunath Prasad Singh v. Chandika Prasad Kumar support treating the unqualified expression “Malik Mustakil” as conferring an absolute estate unless other words or circumstances qualify it.

predicates.compromise_deed_uses_unqualified_absolut: The deed describes the recipient’s ownership of the allotted property in unqualified terms of absolute ownership.
predicates.deed_context_does_not_qualify_grant: The circumstances surrounding the deed do not indicate that the recipient’s ownership is limited.

issues.definition: When a deed uses unqualified language of absolute ownership and its context does not limit that grant, the recipient receives an absolute estate.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not invalidate a compromise on a ground that the parties did not raise in their pleadings.
material_facts: The plaintiffs did not plead that the compromise was illegal.
There was no issue framed on the compromise’s validity.
The High Court held the compromise illegal and relied on that conclusion to reject its effect.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in deciding that the compromise was illegal when that challenge had not been pleaded.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the validity of the compromise was not properly open for decision because the plaintiffs had not raised the issue in their pleadings. It also distinguished compromises with presumptive reversioners from compromises with third parties, relying on the principles discussed in Dhyan Singh v. Jugal Kishore.

predicates.civil_property_dispute: The proceeding is a civil dispute concerning rights in property.
predicates.compromise_validity_not_pleaded: The party challenging the compromise did not plead that it was invalid.
predicates.no_issue_framed_on_validity: The court did not frame an issue for deciding the compromise’s validity.

issues.definition: In a civil property dispute, when compromise validity was neither pleaded nor made an issue, the court must not decide an unpleaded validity challenge.

issues.legal_issue: Reversioners who enter a compromise with a widow in return for her relinquishing claims to other property are estopped from later challenging her alienation of the property allotted to her absolutely.
material_facts: The widow claimed a right to enjoy the property during her lifetime and relinquished a substantial part of it under the compromise.
The presumptive reversioners agreed to give her an absolute interest in the portion allotted to her in return for that relinquishment.
The widow relied on that representation and later alienated the allotted property.
The reversioners later challenged the alienations; their sons claimed through them and had no independent right in the property.
issues.conclusion: The reversioners who were parties to the compromise were estopped from challenging the alienations, and their sons could not advance a claim through them.
issues.legal_principle: A widow cannot enlarge her estate through a compromise with third parties to the prejudice of ultimate reversioners, but a compromise with persons who become the reversioners may estop those persons from resiling from it. The Court treated the promise to confer an absolute interest in exchange for relinquishment as a representation of fact on which the widow relied to her detriment. It relied on Dhyan Singh v. Jugal Kishore and T. V. R. Subbu Chetty’s Family Charities v. M. Raghava Mudaliar.

predicates.suit_challenges_alienation_by_widow: The proceeding seeks to challenge an alienation made by a widow.
predicates.compromise_with_presumptive_reversioners: The widow made the compromise with persons who were presumptive reversioners to the estate.
predicates.widow_relinquished_substantial_claim_in_: The widow gave up a substantial claim after the other parties represented that she would receive an absolute interest in part of the property.
predicates.challengers_are_parties_or_claim_only_th: The challengers were parties to the compromise or assert rights only through persons who were parties to it.

issues.definition: When a widow’s alienation is challenged by compromise parties or those claiming through them, and she relinquished a substantial claim in reliance on their promise of an absolute grant, the reversioners are estopped from challenging the alienation.

issues.legal_issue: A settlement of a property dispute between near relations may be a family arrangement even if all participants do not belong to one family in the narrow legal sense.
material_facts: The principal parties to the compromise were near relations.
The dispute concerned property originally owned by their common ancestor.
The compromise settled the parties’ competing claims to that property.
issues.conclusion: The compromise could be treated as a family arrangement, and the suits challenging the resulting alienations were not maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: The word “family” in the context of a family arrangement is not confined to persons with a legal right of succession or a claim to a share in the disputed property. A settlement of a dispute between near relations may qualify. Courts favour family arrangements to preserve harmony and prevent future disputes. The Court relied on Ram Charan Das v. Girjanandini Devi and Sahu Madho Das v. Pandit Mukand Ram.

predicates.civil_property_dispute_between_near_rela: The proceeding concerns a property dispute between people who are near relations.
predicates.dispute_concerns_property_of_common_ance: The disputed property originally belonged to an ancestor common to the parties.
predicates.settlement_resolves_competing_claims: The parties settled their competing claims to the disputed property.

issues.definition: A settlement resolving a property dispute between near relations over property of a common ancestor qualifies as a family arrangement.

issues.legal_issue: A plea of estoppel may be considered despite the absence of a specifically labelled plea in the written statement when its substance is pleaded, the framed issue covers it, and it has been considered without objection.
material_facts: The written statement asserted that the plaintiffs were bound by the compromise and had no right to deny the widow’s rights over the sold properties.
A framed issue asked whether the plaintiffs were bound by the compromise and what its effect was.
The plea of estoppel was argued and considered by the courts without objection from the plaintiffs.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs could not object that estoppel was unavailable merely because the written statement did not specifically label it as a plea of estoppel.
issues.legal_principle: A plea may be considered when the substance of the defence appears in the pleadings, the framed issue is broad enough to encompass it, and the parties argued and litigated it without objection.

rule.if: civil_property_proceeding and pleading_asserts_claimant_bound_by_compromise and framed_issue_covers_effect_of_compromise and estoppel_litigated_without_objection

predicates.civil_property_proceeding: The proceeding is a civil dispute concerning property rights.
predicates.pleading_asserts_claimant_bound_by_compr: A pleading asserts that the claimant is bound by the compromise and cannot deny the rights it recognizes.
predicates.framed_issue_covers_effect_of_compromise: A framed issue asks whether the claimant is bound by the compromise or what effect it has.
predicates.estoppel_litigated_without_objection: The parties argued and the courts considered estoppel without an objection that it had not been specifically pleaded.

issues.definition: In a civil property proceeding, a court may consider estoppel without a specific label in the pleading when the defence’s substance is pleaded, the framed issue covers the compromise’s effect, and estoppel was litigated without objection.
